title: A WAV header reader
description:
Sound files in WAV format start with a 44-byte header. Write `read_wav_header(data: bytes) -> dict` that checks and reads it:

| offset | size | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 4 | `b"RIFF"` |
| 4 | 4 | file size minus 8 (unsigned, little-endian) |
| 8 | 4 | `b"WAVE"` |
| 12 | 4 | `b"fmt "` |
| 16 | 4 | 16 for plain audio |
| 20 | 2 | format, 1 means PCM |
| 22 | 2 | channels |
| 24 | 4 | sample rate |
| 28 | 4 | bytes per second |
| 32 | 2 | block align |
| 34 | 2 | bits per sample |
| 36 | 4 | `b"data"` |
| 40 | 4 | size of the sound data |

Return `{"channels", "sample_rate", "bits", "data_size", "seconds"}`, where `seconds` is `data_size / bytes per second` rounded to 3 places. Raise `ValueError` for data shorter than 44 bytes, any wrong marker, a format other than 1, or a bytes-per-second value that does not equal `sample_rate * channels * bits // 8`.
hints: One `struct.Struct("<4sI4s4sIHHIIHH4sI")` matches the whole table: `4s` for each marker, `I` for 4-byte numbers, `H` for 2-byte ones. Its `.size` is 44.
`unpack_from(data)` reads from the start of a longer buffer without needing an exact length.
